questions.topic: Counting semitones with a flat on the upper note
questions.learningObjective: Order intervals with a flattened upper note by semitone count.

stimulus.body: Read this source excerpt carefully: The counts are two, three, four and eight semitones, so that is the running order. A marginal reminder adds: count each pair with its flat in place. It is followed by four candidate interpretations, of which exactly one is supported by the wording of the excerpt.

questions.stem: The rule to carry into this item is “Order intervals with a flattened upper note by semitone count. / Count each pair with its flat in place. / Counting semitones…”. Which option applies it?

options.text: D4 up to F flat 4, then C4 up to F flat 4, then G4 up to B flat 4, then B flat 4 up to G flat 5

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Counting semitones in a fifth reached with a sharp
questions.learningObjective: Describe a fifth whose two notes both carry a sharp.

stimulus.body: The working note below records the evidence for a claim about counting semitones in a fifth reached with a sharp. sharpening both notes of a fifth leaves the interval the same width, so F sharp up to C sharp is a perfect fifth of seven semitones. A marginal reminder adds: ask what happens when both notes move up together. A reader must decide which of the four proposed statements the note warrants, without using outside knowledge.

questions.stem: Read this item with “Describe a fifth whose two notes both carry a sharp. / Ask what happens when both notes move up together. / Counting semitones in…” as the standard. Which choice qualifies?

options.text: A major sixth of nine semitones, because the letters cover six names
options.misconception: Counts the letter span as a sixth by mistake.

options.text: An augmented fifth of eight semitones, because the sharps widen the interval
options.misconception: Widens the fifth even though both notes are raised together.

options.text: A diminished fifth of six semitones, because the sharp on the lower note narrows it
options.misconception: Applies the lower-note rule when both notes are sharped.

options.text: A perfect fifth of seven semitones, since both notes carry the same sharp

questions.explanation: Sharpening both notes of a fifth leaves the interval the same width, so F sharp up to C sharp is a perfect fifth of seven semitones. Sharpening only one of the notes is what changes the size.
questions.hint: Ask what happens when both notes move up together.
